name: HubSpot

auth.keyHelp: In HubSpot go to Development, Keys, Service keys, Create service key, and add only crm.objects.contacts.read and crm.objects.deals.read for read-only use.

tested: mock; real service refused a fake key
notes: Surprise: legacy private apps (the old 'private app access token') can no longer be created (disabled 2026-09-28 for new accounts, 2026-10-26 for older ones; existing ones keep working). HubSpot now says to use SERVICE KEYS for in-account integrations: created in HubSpot under Development > Keys > Service keys > Create service key; super admins and users with Developer tools access can create them; example key starts pat-na1-; sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'; REST only; scopes are object-specific (crm.objects.contacts.read, etc.) so read-only is possible; optional auto-rotation every 3, 6 or 12 months. The page does NOT state which plans or tiers include service keys. There is no direct issuing URL because the page lives inside the user's own portal, so keyUrl points to the docs page that describes the steps. API paths are date-versioned: the 2026-09 specs are used here (paths like /crm/objects/2026-09/contacts; deals use object type id 0-3). The older /crm/v3/objects/... paths still appear in HubSpot's guides. Scopes seen in the specs: crm.objects.contacts.write and crm.objects.deals.write for writes; read scopes crm.objects.deals.read etc. (the contacts list spec lists several accepted read scopes). The account-info details spec shows an empty security list, so no scope is required by the spec, but the guide's scope section could not be read; treat as unconfirmed. Test response fields: portalId, accountType, timeZone, uiDomain, companyCurrency, dataHostingLocation. Official remote MCP server https://mcp.hubspot.com needs OAuth with PKCE (S256, required): the user first creates an MCP connector in their own HubSpot account to get a client ID and secret, then the MCP client runs the sign-in flow; a service key is not an MCP credential.
